transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-12 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Meyers (Nimbus Head of Platform), Sofia Ramos (Nimbus MLOps), Damien Cole (Finance), Lee Park (Security)

Summary: quick console walkthrough focused on per-route dashboards for usage, token-level cost breakdown, exporting billing reports, and how Redwood Optimize recommendations show up in the console. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for cost predictability; primary concerns are multi-route attribution, audit logs, and SSO.

Topics: per-route dashboards; token/cost breakdowns; query-level tracing; Optimize suggestions for batching and caching; export formats; security/compliance (SOC2, KMS); pilot next steps.

Action items (captured verbally during call): see metadata.

00:00:00 - Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we can kick off, thanks Jordan for coordinating. quick intro — i'm Alex, i'm the AE, with Priya our solutions engineer.
00:00:12 - Jordan Meyers: yeah thanks Alex, uh excited to see how the console maps our multiple routes to billing, Damien from finance wants to know if we can get per-feature cost breakdowns.
00:00:23 - Damien Cole: hi all, quick one — our CFO needs monthly reports that show cost per product route, and ideally an exported CSV for internal chargebacks.
00:00:30 - Priya Kapoor: great, that's exactly what the per-route dashboard is built for. we'll walk through live, i'll highlight the route filters, token buckets, and the cost attribution logic which is per-request multiplied by effective tokens and model unit price, plus any dedicated overhead.
00:00:50 - Lee Park: also from security: how are audit logs surfaced and retained? we have a 7-year retention requirement for some logs, so curious whether console exports or we need to push to our SIEM.
00:01:02 - Priya Kapoor: good question — right now console stores detailed traces for 90 days in the UI; for long term retention we provide an export endpoint and integrations to push to S3 / our audit log export job. we also support streaming audit events to a customer's Kinesis or PubSub. (mild stutter) sorry — Kinesis or pub-sub depending on region.
00:01:25 - Jordan Meyers: nice, okay show us the per-route view.
00:01:30 - Priya Kapoor: ok switching to the console — starting at the main Routes screen, you can see each route with its QPS, 95th latency, and estimated monthly cost. clicking into a route opens the route dashboard: top section is traffic and latency, middle is model usage and token distribution, bottom is cost breakdown and recent requests sample.
00:01:55 - 00:02:10 - (audio glitch) Speaker labelled as Speaker 1: [inaudible] -- looks like a network hiccup for a sec.
00:02:12 - Priya Kapoor: sorry about that, continuing — cost breakdown has three rows: model spend, infra surcharge (if you're on Dedicated there's a committed capacity line), and auxiliary features like streaming or advanced logging. the UI shows cost both by absolute dollars and normalized per-1k tokens for quick comparison.
00:02:35 - Sofia Ramos: how is the 1k token cost calculated for different models? we run gpt-style and some quantized smaller models across routes.
00:02:44 - Priya Kapoor: we surface effective unit price per model variant — baseline is model unit price from the catalog times a small routing multiplier if you have dedicated pools or cross-region routing. quantized variants show lower per-token compute but you can see a quality delta in the quality tab, which helps decide tradeoffs.
00:03:02 - Priya Kapoor: also we have a per-route override if you want specific routes to always use a particular model or quantization profile — useful for latency sensitive paths.
00:03:15 - Jordan Meyers: can we tag routes for product owners? we need chargebacks for teams.
00:03:20 - Alex Chen: absolutely — routes support tags and a cost-center field. exports include tags so finance can ingest it for chargebacks.
00:03:28 - Damien Cole: perfect, does the export include token breakdown by prompt vs completion?
00:03:33 - Priya Kapoor: yes, CSV includes prompt tokens, completion tokens, model id, route id, timestamp, and cost columns. note the per-request sample in UI is sanitized if you have PII redaction enabled.
00:03:47 - Lee Park: about PII — is redaction deterministic and where does that happen? we can't have PII leave our VPC for our private deployment plan.
00:03:55 - Priya Kapoor: for Redwood Private we provide an on-prem agent and the redaction happens pre-send in the customer network; for hosted we do optional client-side redaction and we also offer a data-in-flight encryption + KMS integration, so the payloads in Redwood logs can be encrypted.
00:04:14 - Jordan Meyers: great. can we walk through a sample route and a spike? show me a 95th latency and how cost changes during burst windows.
00:04:22 - Priya Kapoor: sure — opening the route dashboard, here's a traffic spike on 7/28, you can see autoscaling events annotated. the cost chart overlays token consumption and billed compute; note that if you exceed reserved capacity you'll see failover to the fallback pool and that may change per-token unit price.
00:04:43 - Alex Chen: quick aside on Optimize — the console will suggest batching thresholds and prefix cache settings per route based on observed token distribution. we can create a recommendation set and enable it in staging first.
00:04:58 - Sofia Ramos: are those Optimize suggestions actionable via API? we want to automate applying suggestions as part of CI.
00:05:04 - Priya Kapoor: yes, there's a recommendations API and a CLI we expose. you can approve a recommendation and it writes the route config via api/v1/routes/<id>/apply-recommendation. (transcription picks up as api slash one slash routes)
00:05:20 - Damian Cole: what about unit economics? give me an example of a monthly bill for a route that serves 50M tokens at mixed models.
00:05:28 - Alex Chen: rough example — if mix is 60% small quantized at $0.3 per 1k and 40% larger at $2.0 per 1k, blended unit price ~ $0.92 per 1k tokens, so 50M tokens ~ 50k 1k units = $46k roughly, plus any dedicated capacity overhead. we'll send a spreadsheet with more exact math.
00:05:55 - 00:06:10 - Jordan Meyers: is there a way to allocate overhead per route for dedicated capacity — so finance can apportion infra costs?
00:06:15 - Priya Kapoor: yes — we support an allocation policy that splits reserved capacity cost by defined weights (route traffic, token consumption, or fixed percentages). the allocation model and weights are in the settings and are included in the exported billing payload.
00:06:31 - Lee Park: SSO question — we have Okta and require SCIM provisioning and attribute mapping. how does console handle RBAC?
00:06:38 - Alex Chen: we support SAML and OIDC SSO flows, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based policies with route-level permissions. you can restrict who can apply recommendations, who can view cost, and who can download exports.
00:06:53 - Sofia Ramos: any guardrails to prevent accidental rollout of a quantized model to prod?
00:06:58 - Priya Kapoor: yes — rollout policies can require multi-stage approval and you can set a hard guardrail that blocks a rollout unless a runbook approval checkbox is checked. we also keep a changelog so you can revert to previous model versions.
00:07:12 - Jordan Meyers: ok walk me through a practical scenario: we have an internal search API route and an email-summarization route. we want search to be low-latency even if cost is higher. email-summarization can be batched and run on cheaper variants.
00:07:25 - Priya Kapoor: perfect example — create two routes, tag them with cost-center/team. set model override on search to high-perf model and on summarization enable batching and 5s response-time tolerance. Optimize will simulate savings and show expected latency impact in the recommendations panel.
00:07:42 - 00:07:56 - (brief cross-talk) Jordan: are there any gotchas for client-side caching? Priya: only if prompt variability is high caching less effective but prefix/KV cache works well for conversation flows.
00:08:00 - Damien Cole: our finance team cares about sudden cost spikes due to new prompt templates — can we set alerts?
00:08:06 - Priya Kapoor: yes — per-route budget alerts, anomalous spend detection (statistical baselines) and you can configure webhook + slack alerts.
00:08:18 - Alex Chen: also there's a simulated billing runner — run it on a sample traffic CSV to get a forecast for next 30/90 days. we'll run that as part of the pilot.
00:08:30 - Jordan Meyers: what's the granularity of the forecast? per route? per model?
00:08:34 - Priya Kapoor: both — forecast can be sliced by route, model, and tag. it uses TTL-adjusted traffic seasonality if you provide week-of-day patterns.
00:08:45 - Sofia Ramos: security again — do you store prompt contents in logs by default?
00:08:50 - Priya Kapoor: by default we store request/response metadata and a sample of recent requests for troubleshooting; full payload retention is off by default and must be enabled with compliance flags. for sensitive customers we recommend Private deployment and client-side redaction.
00:09:06 - Damien Cole: can we have a delayed export where we only pull logs after 30 days for compliance?
00:09:11 - Priya Kapoor: yes exports can be scheduled or triggered via retention policies.
00:09:18 - Alex Chen: let's demo one export — i'm going to click route export, select csv, date range last 30 days, include tags and token breakdown. starting export... (typing sounds) CSV ready, link appears; i'll share it in the notes after the call.
00:09:38 - 00:10:02 - (background typing / link pasted) Alex Chen: posted link to meeting notes with the export sample and a short walkthrough video.
00:10:10 - Jordan Meyers: nice. couple of gotchas — we run some in-house small models on our infra; can Redwood route requests to an on-prem adapter so we can keep some models in our cluster?
00:10:20 - Priya Kapoor: yes — that's the Private hybrid mode; we can route via a connector, and the console will show hybrid inventory. you'll see mixed model catalog entries and cost accounting will include either notional compute credit or pass-through billing depending on contract.
00:10:36 - Sofia Ramos: on that, how do we handle version pinning and rollouts for hybrid models?
00:10:40 - Priya Kapoor: same lifecycle — you pin a model version, create rollout policy, and the console manages traffic split; the difference is the runtime confirms compatibility with the on-prem adapter and the model checksum.
00:10:55 - Damien Cole: from a procurement perspective how are invoicing and commitments handled for Dedicated? do you show monthly amortized costs?
00:11:02 - Alex Chen: yes committed capacity invoices show amortization schedules and we provide a monthly line-item export for accounting. we'll include a sample invoice in the follow-up packet.
00:11:14 - 00:11:30 - Jordan Meyers: any latency SLO metrics we can surface in the console per route?
00:11:34 - Priya Kapoor: 95/99 latency histograms, P99 tail and percentile heatmaps; you can set SLO alerts and correlate with model version or region.
00:11:48 - Lee Park: can we restrict who sees cost vs who sees metrics?
00:11:51 - Alex Chen: yes separate RBAC scopes — cost-view only and full-admin.
00:11:58 - Sofia Ramos: how do you calculate inferred cost for caching and prefix hits?
00:12:04 - Priya Kapoor: we log cache hits and treat them as lower compute cost; the console shows cache hit ratio and an estimated cost-savings metric that rolls into the per-route billing projection.
00:12:18 - Damien Cole: are discounts applied regionally?
00:12:22 - Alex Chen: discounts are contract-level but we can show regional breakdown and apply a contract-level multiplier to the exported numbers.
00:12:31 - Jordan Meyers: i'd like to see the recommendation view for our three chosen routes. can we set up a pilot with data feed?
00:12:37 - Priya Kapoor: absolutely — pilot package: 2-week run with recommendations enabled, a runbook, and a review session where we go line-by-line on savings. we'll need a sample traffic CSV and expected production latency constraints.
00:12:52 - Alex Chen: i'll follow up with a kickoff invite for next week.
00:12:55 - 00:13:20 - (noise) brief pause while people review exported CSV.
00:13:25 - Jordan Meyers: quick question — if we use the recommendation to enable batching, does it change request semantics for callers?
00:13:31 - Priya Kapoor: batching is at the route layer — small change: requests may be buffered up to configured window (e.g., 50ms-5s). we provide a batched response wrapper and a per-request id mapping, so callers can map back results. semantics preserved, but latency can increase.
00:13:50 - Damien Cole: finance wants guaranteed cost ceilings per route — any hard caps?
00:13:55 - Priya Kapoor: yes you can set hard budget caps that throttle or reject requests once the cap is met, or optionally divert traffic to a cheaper fallback model.
00:14:08 - Lee Park: any certifications we should be aware of for SEC or healthcare?
00:14:12 - Alex Chen: we have SOC 2 Type II and are working toward ISO 27001; for HIPAA / healthcare customers we offer Private deployments and BAAs.
00:14:24 - Jordan Meyers: great. last thing — will you include a simple math example in the follow-up so Finance can see line-by-line?
00:14:30 - Alex Chen: yes, we'll include a sample calc and the exported CSV.
00:14:35 - Jordan Meyers: thanks, this is useful. any other questions?
00:14:38 - Sofia Ramos: can you also include the CLI snippet to pull the recommendation via API?
00:14:43 - Priya Kapoor: sure, i'll paste a snippet in notes.
00:14:48 - Alex Chen: ok we'll wrap up — next steps as discussed: send materials, schedule pilot kickoff for next week, Nimbus to provide traffic samples. thanks everyone.
00:14:59 - (meeting wraps; some small chatter)

Notes / Links shared: route-export-sample.csv (link), pilot-runbook-template.md (link), SOC2-summary.pdf (link), recommendation-api-snippet.txt (link).

End of transcript.
